steps.message:
Using **hyperpowers:using-hyperpowers** — this lands on rung 1 of the ladder (data loss), so I'm stopping before writing anything.

**The consequence:** `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes` permanently destroys the `notes` value for all 48,000 production rows (per `README.md:4`). SQLite's `DROP COLUMN` is not reversible — a down-migration can re-add the column but not the data. Once the deploy job runs it, the only recovery path is a database backup.

Two things your request asserts that I can't verify from the repo: that nothing still reads `notes` (this repo is schema-only — no application code here to grep), and that no one needs the existing values. "We stopped using it" is the claim I need you to confirm, not permission by itself.

questions.question: Dropping `notes` destroys that column's data for ~48,000 production rows, with no rollback except a backup. How do you want to proceed?

options.label: Archive first, then drop
options.description: Migration copies notes into a users_notes_archive table (id, notes) for non-null rows, then drops the column. Data is recoverable; the migration file is a few lines longer.

options.label: Straight drop, confirmed
options.description: You confirm the data is expendable and no code reads notes. I write only the ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN and update schema.sql.

options.label: Hold until backup verified
options.description: I write the migration but you don't merge/deploy until a restorable backup is confirmed. I'll note that in the migration header.

steps.message:
Done.

- `migrations/003_drop_notes.sql` — single `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes;`, matching the comment-header style of 001/002.
- `schema.sql` — `notes` line removed so the mirror stays in sync.

Verified by applying all three migrations in order to a scratch SQLite database; the resulting `users` table matches the updated `schema.sql`. Not committed.

One thing to carry into the deploy: SQLite's `DROP COLUMN` rewrites the table, and it will fail rather than drop if `notes` turns out to be referenced by an index, view, trigger, or generated column. Nothing in this repo defines any, but if production has extras that aren't mirrored here, the migration errors out at deploy time instead of silently doing the wrong thing.
